# Document Audit Policy Report

_2026-09-27 · Devin · live-verified against ada-cms-pages (40 pages)_

## Why this exists

Ada generates CMS pages through `cms_publish_page`, and until today
there was **no quality gate** — the first news-* batch shipped with
missing H1s, no source links, no "why it matters", and nobody could
tell without eyeballing every page. An audit rule-set now exists
(`chaba/scripts/ada/cms-audit.py`, committed `9f9eadb4`) plus a
tightened format spec (`news-system` page).

## The policy — what a page must satisfy

### Generic rules (all `kind: page` docs)

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| A1 | Body non-empty, ≥ 200 chars — *the empty-shell bug (`content_md` vs `contentMd`) is exactly what this catches* |
| A2 | Meta complete: `slug`, `title`, `format`, `updated`, `kind=page` |
| A3 | H1 heading present and matching the page title |
| A4 | Real structure — headings or lists, not a bare paragraph blob |
| A5 | No placeholders (TODO / TBD / lorem / placeholder) |
| A6 | No secret-shaped strings (`api_key=`, `password:`, …) |

### News brief rules (`news-*` pages only)

| Rule | Requirement |
|---|---|
| N1 | `TL;DR:` line — one sentence, concrete |
| N2 | ≤ 6 items per page |
| N3 | `[Source](url)` link per item |
| N4 | `Why it matters:` per item |

The full contract lives on the `news-system` page — Ada reads it before
drafting, so tightening the spec is the lever that improves output.

## What the first audit found (before → after)

| Group | Result |
|---|---|
| All 40 pages | 34 pass / **11 fail** |
| news-* (6 pages) | **all 6 failed**: missing H1 ×4, no sources ×4, no why-it-matters ×3, no TL;DR ×1 |

Fix loop that ran today:
1. `news_pages_update` scenario — Ada updated all 5 news pages (PASS
   on handshake/flow, but content failed audit).
2. Spec tightened → `news-system` now lists *required* elements.
3. `news_audit_fix` scenario — Ada re-drafted under the spec; 3 pages
   landed compliant, `news-world` got eaten by the pending-confirm
   handshake (she believed it published — it didn't), `news-thailand`
   was outside the fix scope.
4. Direct repair on the stragglers → **final audit: 6/6 news pass,
   37/40 overall** (remaining fails: `todo-list`, `idea-summary`,
   `cached-videos-report`, `vcast-failure-report`, `devin-job-report-fail`
   — mostly old/placeholder pages, deliberately left).

## Findings worth keeping

- **Pending-confirm can swallow a publish silently** — Ada thinks it
  landed; verify-after-publish should be mandatory, not optional
  (news-system now says so).
- **Ada invents structure per session** unless the spec is hard.
  "House style" as prose → soft compliance; as numbered MUSTs → she
  hit it on the first retry for 3/4 pages.
- **The audit is runnable cheaply** — `python3 scripts/ada/cms-audit.py
  [prefix]`, ~1s against mddb. Hookable into the scenario runner's
  ExecStopPost alongside lab-results.

## GitHub knowledge applied

- **errata-ai/vale** + `elastic/vale-rules` — the prose-linter model:
  our A-rules are a lighter, zero-dependency version (Vale itself is
  overkill for a 40-page CMS but is the upgrade path if the corpus
  grows).
- **GitHub Docs content linter** (markdownlint-based, custom rules on
  top) — the pattern we copied: stock rules *plus* collection-specific
  rules (N-rules), warning vs error severity.
- **lychee** (link checking) — not implemented yet; N3 checks link
  *presence*, a future pass could check link *liveness*.
- Microsoft code-with playbook / docs-as-code practice — "docs get the
  same gates as code" is the framing: audit on publish, not on review.

## Suggested next steps

1. Wire `cms-audit.py` into `ada-scenario-smoke`'s ExecStopPost (next to
   lab-results.py) so every suite run re-audits.
2. Add a `cms_audit` tool for Ada — she could self-check before asking
   you to confirm a publish.
3. Extend rules: image/link liveness, stale-date warnings on living
   pages (todo-list class), Thai-language pages pass fine today but a
   bilingual style rule may be worth pinning.

# Project Analysis: V-Cast Interface & Automation Failures **Target:** Devin coding session & Ada RCA study. ## Problem Statement Ongoing issues impact user confidence in the WeCast system and automated home controls. ## Known Failures 1. ### Visual Failures (V-Cast) - Screen 1 ownership logic prevents public access. - Content fails to render (broken image icon). 2. ### Automation Loop Failures - Unexpected TV plug activation triggers. ## Devin Action Plan - [x] Analyze `chaba` PWA receiver logic for broken image handling. — DONE 2026-09-28 - [ ] Review Home Assistant logbook for plug trigger source context. --- ## Repair Outcome — 2026-09-28 (Devin dispatch, chaba) **Broken image icon — root causes found & fixed:** 1. **Scheme**: the casted URL used `http://` on `:8123`, an HTTPS-only listener (plain HTTP → bare 400). On the HTTPS receiver page it was also mixed-content blocked. Fixed: receiver's `mediaUrl()` upgrades `http:`→`https:` media URLs. 2. **Missing file**: `/local/documents/A-68/...jpg` 404s even over HTTPS on both HA instances — that path was never published (A-68 pages live only in the idc01 doc-archive, behind `X-API-Key`, unusable as ``). 3. Image load failures now surface: HUD "image failed" + toast + `state:error` to the relay (previously a silent broken icon). **"Ada can't see the cast screen" — fixed:** - Snapshot path (`snap-request` → canvas → `/frame` → `vcast_snapshot`) was live but died on cross-origin `` (tainted canvas SecurityError). New relay endpoint `GET /img?url=` (tailnet/LAN allowlisted) lets the display refetch the URL server-side so pixels stay readable. Live-verified: casting the HA cam jpg to screen 2 now returns a real 424×240 JPEG frame. - Webpage (`nav`) casts verified working on screen 2; cross-origin iframes honestly report `uncapturable-iframe` + page URL — Ada can name the page, can't screenshot it (browser security, not a bug). **Deployed:** receiver `index.html` → live web mount; `server.mjs` → idc01 `input-bridge` (restarted). iPad (screen 1) picks up the new build on next connect. **Still open:** - Screen-1 owner-lock complaint (public screen treated as private) — separate ada-pi `cast-screens.json` ACL issue, not addressed here. - `/local/documents/` publishing decision (options logged in chaba job record `2026-09-28-vcast-image-mixed-content`). - TV plug automation trigger — not investigated.

จากการตรวจสอบข้อมูลเบื้องต้นเกี่ยวกับบริการรถยกฟรีในเขตบางพลี จังหวัดสมุทรปราการ ในช่วงสถานการณ์น้ำท่วม มีข้อมูลที่สำคัญดังนี้:

## หน่วยงานให้บริการ
*   **บก.จร. (กองบังคับการตำรวจจราจร):** มีการประชาสัมพันธ์ให้บริการรถยกฟรีเพื่อช่วยเหลือประชาชนในการเคลื่อนย้ายรถยนต์ที่ประสบปัญหาน้ำท่วมขัง โดยเน้นการเคลื่อนย้ายหลังจากระดับน้ำลดลงแล้ว สามารถติดต่อสอบถามข้อมูลเพิ่มเติมได้ที่สายด่วนตำรวจจราจร 1197

## ข้อแนะนำเพิ่มเติม
*   ประชาชนที่ต้องการความช่วยเหลือควรเตรียมข้อมูลสถานที่ที่รถจอดอยู่และจุดหมายที่ต้องการให้พ่วงลากไปให้ชัดเจน
*   ควรรวบรวมข้อมูลหน่วยงานท้องถิ่นอื่นๆ เช่น เทศบาล หรือ อบต. ในพื้นที่บางพลี ที่อาจมีมาตรการช่วยเหลือเพิ่มเติมในช่วงวิกฤต

# Gemini Deep Research agent — capability assessment for Chaba/Ada

Date: 2026-09-27 · Sources: ai.google.dev deep-research & interactions docs, Google dev blog (Dec 2025), AI Studio forum

## What it is

Google's autonomous research agent, exposed to developers via the **Interactions API**
(the new GA single endpoint for models *and* agents — `generateContent` is now legacy).
Three agents:

| Agent id | Character | Est. cost/task |
|---|---|---|
| `deep-research-preview-04-2026` | fast, streamable, ~80 queries / ~250k in / ~60k out | ~$1–3 |
| `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` | max comprehensiveness, ~160 queries / ~900k in / ~80k out | ~$3–7 |
| `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` | older Gemini 3.1 Pro version | — |

Powered by Gemini 3 Pro (SOTA on HLE + DeepSearchQA per Google; best-on-BrowseComp claim).
DeepSearchQA benchmark itself is open-sourced — usable for our own evals.

## API shape

- `interactions.create` with `agent=deep-research-*`, **`background=true` required**,
  `store=true` (retention: 55d paid / 1d free tier)
- Poll `interaction_id` until `completed`/`failed`, or `stream=true` for live steps
- `collaborative_planning=True` → agent returns a research *plan* first; a follow-up
  turn confirms/edits it before execution — **this maps 1:1 onto our confirm gates**
- `visualization="auto"` → generates charts/graphs inline in the report
- `tools` override: `google_search`, `external_data_mcp` (**it can call MCP servers**),
  `vertex_search`, File Upload/File Search for private docs (PDF/CSV)
- `service_tier="deferred"` → off-peak scheduling at **50% discount**
- Multiple concurrent background tasks allowed; label `is_deep_research` tracks cost

## Fit with our stack

### Ada voice tool — `ada_deep_research(topic, depth="standard"|"max")`

Natural fit for the dispatch/awaiting-user model:

1. Ada registers an MDDB job doc + starts interaction (`background`, `store`)
2. She answers immediately: "research queued, job X — I'll tell you when it lands"
3. A watcher (or poll-on-ask via `ada_deep_research_status`) detects completion
4. Report → `cms_publish_page` (via the new pending-confirm handshake for publish) +
   extract summary into memory bank + notify via `/api/notify`
5. Verification: CMS slug + interaction_id recorded on the job doc

The `collaborative_planning` option is the interesting one for voice: Ada reads the
plan aloud, Tony says "yes" or edits it, then she proceeds — exactly the
confirmation pattern we already want.

### Devin dispatch lanes

For project research (codebases, vendor comparisons): the dispatch JSONL ledger
already models long-running jobs — DR calls could be steps inside dispatched
sessions rather than separate plumbing.

### NotebookLM

DR is coming to NotebookLM natively — overlaps our NotebookLM summarization path;
watch for it replacing our digest step rather than duplicating it.

### Benchmarking

DeepSearchQA (open-source, Google) = a real benchmark corpus for complex web
research — could score Ada's `web_search`+synthesis path against DR directly.

## Constraints / watch-outs

- **Preview** — agents ids are dated previews; expect churn
- **Paid tier required** — our key is free tier now (web_search hit the 20/day
  grounding cap today); DR has no free quota worth using; also API keys must be
  restricted to generativelanguage.googleapis.com by June 2026 policy
- Runs take **minutes** — never inline on a live voice turn; always background
- Retention: free=1d (too short for our job ledger), paid=55d — we must snapshot
  the report to MDDB/CMS on completion regardless
- `store=true` means queries live on Google's side — no sensitive content in prompts

## Recommendation

Yes — adopt as Ada's `ada_deep_research` tool (standard tier default, `max` opt-in,
`deferred` when not urgent). It's the strongest missing piece between quick
`web_search` and full Devin dispatch: ~$1–3 for a cited multi-source report lands
squarely in our "control desk → job → notify → verify" architecture.

Prereqs: paid-tier API key (restricted scope), watcher for completion,
CMS publish on land. MVP ~half a day of plumbing.

# Gemini & OR Embedding Benchmark

Run 2026-09-28T04:33:00Z — 29 real `ada-cms-pages` docs, 768 dims.
Direct = `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` batchEmbedContents;
OR = `google/gemini-embedding-2` via OpenRouter (provider order: Google Vertex).

## Verdict

**Same vector space — OR is a drop-in mirror, safe to keep.**

| metric | direct Gemini | OpenRouter |
|---|---|---|
| latency p50 (10-doc batch) | 1.87s | 10.42s |
| latency worst batch | 2.01s | 10.58s |
| top-1 retrieval probes | 8/8 | 8/8 |

cosine(OR, direct) per doc — mean **1.0**, min **1.0**
(≈1.0 = identical space; same underlying model via Vertex).

## Cost

- OR billed tokens this run: **10711** ≈ **$0.00161**
  (at $0.15/Mtok — recheck OR pricing if it shifts).
- Projected: mddb daily writes ≈ tens of docs → **< $0.01/month** steady state;
  full-corpus re-embed ≈ a few cents one-shot.
- Comparison for *search* (not embeddings): Gemini paid grounding is
  ~$35/1K queries vs OR online/sonar routes ~$4-5/1K — the bigger
  argument for OR lives there; free-tier grounding stays at 20/day.

## Routes measured

- Primary (live): `gemini-ollama-proxy` → OR `google/gemini-embedding-2`
- Backup chain in proxy: OR → direct Gemini → local Ollama (`nomic-embed-text`)
- Hard-fail on OR error is deliberate — a different-space fallback would
  poison retrieval silently.

## Pros & cons of keeping OR in parallel

**Pros**
- Same vector space proven (cosine 1.000) — OR is a true mirror, no
  re-embed or collection migration ever needed.
- Off the Gemini free tier — embeddings no longer share the 20-req/day
  budget with grounded `web_search` and voice traffic.
- Predictable spend: measured **$0.0016/run**; steady state < $0.01/mo.
- Chain stays intact on OR outage: OR → (direct Gemini) → local Ollama.

**Cons**
- ~5× slower per batch — OR's Vertex route rejects array input, so every
  text is its own HTTP call (fine at our write volume). OR docs claim
  arrays are supported; the pin to provider `Google` is what breaks it.
- Silent spend creep — needs an occasional usage check, not alerts.
- OR AI-Studio provider route is broken (bogus API_KEY_INVALID) —
  pinned `order:[Google]` is the only working path.

## Improvements — applied vs open

**Applied this run**
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` restored in `mddb-gemini.env` + proxy now falls back
  to direct Gemini (same space, verified 1.000) on OR failure — Ollama
  still refused. Failover tested live: dead OR → direct Gemini → 768d.
- **int8 quantization set on all 40 collections** (`/v1/collection-config`).
  Applies to new writes + the in-memory index; existing float32 storage
  stays readable.

**Live observations during rollout**
- The cold-start vector-index rebuild took **>75 min at ~96% CPU** on
  ~11.6K vectors / 3.4GB DB — vector-search 503s the entire time
  (500+ failed calls; Ada semantic recall degraded during rebuilds).
  Cold-index rebuild is mddb's main operational weakness on this host.
- mddb flagged **18 collections with stale embedding provenance**
  (pre-gemini-embedding-2 space) and auto-re-embeds them through the
  proxy at ~2 calls/min — OR-sequential latency again.
- `POST /v1/vector-reindex` exists and is cheap to call.

**Open (ranked)**
1. **Scheduled `vector-reindex` for the 18 mismatched collections**
   (provenance cleanup — do during off-hours; costs pennies in OR).
2. **OR search tier for `web_search`** — paid Gemini grounding ≈ $35/1K
   vs OR sonar ≈ $5/1K; sits between free-20/day and DuckDuckGo.
3. **Chunk-size tuning** — mddb chunks at 1500 chars; each chunk is one
   sequential OR call → the 20s+ CMS write times. Larger chunks or
   proxy concurrency would cut it.
4. **Parallelize OR embed calls** (4-8 concurrent) in the proxy.
5. **Weekly `embed-bench` timer + OR usage readout.**
6. **Pin `dimensions:768` + model in SSOT.**
7. **OR Batch API** exists for embeddings (async, `provider.only` pin)
   — right tool for bulk re-embeds, not live writes.

## Sources

- mddb quantization: github.com/tradik/mddb → docs/QUANTIZATION.md
- mddb chunking/cache: docs/features + EMBEDDING_PROVIDERS.md
- OR embeddings spec: openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/embeddings
- OR batch API: openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart

# Gesture UI — ada_v2 complete implementation reference + YOLO assessment

Self-contained reference for rebuilding the ada_v2 hand-gesture UI. Everything
needed is in this file — no re-digging the archive required.

**Source of truth:** `tonezzz/ada` (archived) @ `af6d57223f72fce68b4d6f47bbfc6a75b7bc0085`
— `ada_v2/src/App.jsx` (gesture pipeline lines ~1068–1558, window manager
~339–413, ~510–536, ~1720–1876, render ~1919–2238), `ada_v2/package.json`,
`ada_v2/electron/main.js`, `ada_v2/src/index.css`,
`ada_v2/src/components/ToolsModule.jsx`, `ada_v2/backend/server.py`,
`ada_v2/hand_gesture_test.py`, `ada_v2/README.md`.

## Architecture at a glance

```
Webcam (getUserMedia 1920x1080)
  -> <video> (hidden, opacity-0)
  -> requestAnimationFrame(predictWebcam)        ~60fps when video on
       |- drawImage -> visible <canvas>          (CAM_01 tile, optional mirror)
       |- every 5th frame -> 640x360 canvas -> JPEG q0.6
       |     -> socket.emit('video_frame')       -> backend ada.py
       |     -> audio_loop.send_frame -> Gemini Live vision  (side-channel)
       '- if handTracking enabled && new video frame:
             detectForVideo -> 21 normalized landmarks
             -> fingertip cursor math -> pinch click / fist drag
             -> cyan skeleton drawn on canvas
```

All gesture interpretation is **browser-local**. The backend never saw gesture
events — the two paths (UI control vs AI vision) are fully independent.

## Dependencies & assets

- `@mediapipe/tasks-vision` `^0.10.22-rc.20250304` (npm dep in package.json)
- WASM runtime loaded from CDN: `FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(
  "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@0.10.0/wasm")` —
  **note the version skew** (CDN pinned @0.10.0 vs npm rc-20250304)
- Model: `/hand_landmarker.task` served from `public/` (~7.8 MB, Google's stock
  HandLandmarker full model)
- React 18, socket.io-client 4.7.4, electron 28, vite 5, lucide-react icons
- Electron: frameless 1920x1080 window (`frame: false`); top bar uses
  `WebkitAppRegion: 'drag'` (mouse-only OS window drag)

## Init sequence (runs once, guarded)

```js
const vision = await FilesetResolver.forVisionTasks(
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@mediapipe/tasks-vision@0.10.0/wasm");
handLandmarkerRef.current = await HandLandmarker.createFromOptions(vision, {
    baseOptions: { modelAssetPath: "/hand_landmarker.task", delegate: "GPU" },
    runningMode: "VIDEO",
    numHands: 1
});
```

- First `fetch('/hand_landmarker.task')` verifies the file exists (logs
  content-type/length) before creating the landmarker.
- Guarded by `handLandmarkerInitStartedRef` — init runs once on mount.
- Success posts "Hand Tracking Ready" to the chat; failure posts the error.

## Capture & loop

- `getUserMedia({ video: { width: ideal 1920, height: ideal 1080,
  aspectRatio: 16/9, deviceId? } })` -> `video.srcObject` -> `play()`.
- `predictWebcam` runs via `requestAnimationFrame` only while `isVideoOn`.
- Guards: bail if `video.readyState < 2` or `videoWidth/Height === 0`
  (prevents MediaPipe crash on cold start).
- Dedup: `video.currentTime !== lastVideoTimeRef` — skips inference on
  repeated frames.
- `detectForVideo(video, performance.now())` — needs monotonic ms timestamp.
- Hand tracking requires **video ON** (`isVideoOn`) **and** the Hand toggle
  (`isHandTrackingEnabled`, default OFF) — two separate switches.
- FPS counter displayed in top bar while video is on.

## Constants (verified from source)

| Constant | Value | Location |
|---|---|---|
| SENSITIVITY | `cursorSensitivity`, default **2.0** | settings slider; center 50% of camera maps to 100% of screen |
| LERP | **0.2** | `smoothedCursorPos += (target - smoothed) * 0.2` |
| SNAP_THRESHOLD | **50 px** | snap cursor to closest interactive element's center |
| UNSNAP_THRESHOLD | **100 px** | hysteresis — must pass 100px to release |
| PINCH threshold | **0.05** | normalized `dist(lm4, lm8)` |
| Drag deadzone | **0.5 px** | ignore wrist deltas below this |
| Transmission | **640x360, JPEG q0.6, every 5th frame** | `video_frame` socket event |
| numHands | **1** | second hand ignored |
| z base | **30** | `getZIndex = 30 + index in zIndexOrder` |

## Cursor math (per detected frame)

```js
rawX   = isCameraFlipped ? 1 - lm8.x : lm8.x;   // optional mirror
normX  = clamp((rawX - 0.5) * SENSITIVITY + 0.5, 0, 1);
normY  = clamp((lm8.y - 0.5) * SENSITIVITY + 0.5, 0, 1);   // y not flipped
target = normX * innerWidth, normY * innerHeight;
smoothed += (target - smoothed) * 0.2;          // lerp
finalX/finalY = smoothed (unless snapped);
```

**Snap hysteresis** — every frame scans
`document.querySelectorAll('button, input, select, .draggable')`, finds the
element whose **rect center** is nearest the cursor; if `dist < 50px` the
cursor locks to that center and the element gets a cyan glow
(`boxShadow 0 0 20px rgba(34,211,238,.6)`, `backgroundColor rgba(6,182,212,.2)`,
`borderColor cyan` — all **inline styles**; `.snap-highlight` class is added
but has no CSS). Releases only when cursor drifts `> 100px` from the snap
point.

## Pinch = click

- `dist(lm4, lm8) < 0.05` in normalized coordinates.
- **Rising edge only**: fires when `isPinchNow && !isPinching` — one click per
  pinch, hold doesn't repeat.
- Hit-test: `document.elementFromPoint(finalX, finalY)` then
  `el.closest('button, input, a, [role="button"]')` -> `.click()`; falls back
  to `el.click()` if no clickable ancestor.
- Consequence: pinch fires `.click()` but **not** mousedown/mouseup — elements
  driven by pointer-down handlers (drag handles, 3D canvas) don't respond to
  pinch. Dragging is fist-only.

## Fist = grab/drag window

```js
isFingerFolded(tip, mcp) = dist(tip, lm0_wrist) < dist(mcp, lm0_wrist)
isFist = folded(8,5) && folded(12,9) && folded(16,13) && folded(20,17)
         // index, middle, ring, pinky — thumb NOT checked
```

- On fist, if no drag active: hit-test cursor against `getBoundingClientRect()`
  of **`['cad','browser','kasa','printer']`** (popup window ids only) — cursor
  inside rect -> `activeDragElement = id`, `bringToFront(id)`, lock wrist pos.
- While fist held: compute **wrist (lm0)** screen pos with the same
  flip/sensitivity/clamp math (no lerp), delta vs last wrist pos; apply via
  `updateElementPosition(id, dx, dy)` when `|dx|>0.5 || |dy|>0.5`.
- Wrist (not fingertip) is used because the wrist doesn't move while forming
  the fist — fingertip would jump.
- Any non-fist frame releases (`activeDragElement = null`). The README's
  "open palm = release" is just the natural non-fist pose.
- `activeDragElement` also drives a green ring highlight on the grabbed window.

## Window manager contract (what gestures manipulate)

- `elementPositions` / `elementSizes` maps; **anchors differ per element**:
  - `chat`: top-center (`translate(-50%,0)`) — x=中心, y=top edge
  - `video`: top-left
  - everything else: center (`translate(-50%,-50%)`)
- `updateElementPosition` clamps to viewport bounds per anchor type
  (margin 0); `clampToViewport` (margin 10, topBar 60) is used for popup
  initial placement.
- `zIndexOrder` array; `getZIndex = 30 + index`; `bringToFront` moves id to
  end of array.
- `fixedElements = ['visualizer','chat','video','tools']` — never mouse-draggable.
- Mouse path: `handleMouseDown` requires `[data-drag-handle]` inside the
  target **unless** modular mode is on; blocks drag start on
  input/button/textarea/canvas. Fist-drag bypasses the handle requirement and
  works anywhere inside the four popup rects.
- Popup visibility toggles (`showCadWindow` etc.) come from socket events
  (`cad_data`, `browser_frame`, `request_print_window`) or ToolsModule buttons.

## DOM contract for a rebuild

- Hidden `<video>` (opacity-0) + visible `<canvas>` (80% opacity, optional
  `scaleX(-1)` mirror) inside a `w-80 aspect-video` tile labeled CAM_01,
  fixed bottom-right, id=`video`, z=20.
- Cursor: `fixed w-6 h-6 border-2 rounded-full pointer-events-none z-[100]`
  cyan ring + white center dot at `{left: cursorPos.x, top: cursorPos.y,
  transform: translate(-50%,-50%)}`; while pinching it gets
  `bg-cyan-400 scale-75` + stronger glow.
- Popup windows: `id={cad|browser|kasa|printer}`, positioned `absolute` at
  `elementPositions[id]` with `translate(-50%,-50%)`, `zIndex: getZIndex(id)`,
  `data-drag-handle` on their header bars for mouse drag.
- Hand toggle: `Hand` icon button in bottom `ToolsModule` toolbar — orange
  border/glow when enabled.
- Settings: `SettingsWindow` exposes `cursorSensitivity` slider +
  `isCameraFlipped` checkbox; **flip is persisted server-side** —
  backend `settings.json` key `camera_flipped`, pushed on `settings` socket
  event, applied via `setIsCameraFlipped`. (Sensitivity stays client-side.)

## Debug/visual aids

- `drawSkeleton`: cyan `HAND_CONNECTIONS` lines on the display canvas at
  native resolution.
- Logging: "Tracking loop running... Hand Found/No Hand" every 100 frames;
  "First hand detection!" once.
- Removed features still referenced: `cursorTrailRef`, `ripples` state,
  "Trail Logic"/"Ripple Effect" comments — dead code, don't port.

## Worked trace with real values

Cursor — index tip `lm8=(0.58, 0.30)`, screen 1920x1080, SENSITIVITY=2.0:

```
norm    = ((0.58-.5)*2+.5, (0.30-.5)*2+.5)  =  (0.66, 0.10)
target  = (1267, 108) px
lerp a=0.2:  f1 (253,22) -> f3 (618,53) -> f6 (935,80) -> ... -> (1267,108)
```

Snap — button center at (1264,198): dist 16px < 50 -> snaps & locks; drift
60px -> still glued (<=100); drift 120px -> unsnaps.

Pinch — `dist(lm4,lm8) = 0.0071 < 0.05` -> rising edge -> elementFromPoint ->
`.closest('button…').click()`.

Fist drag — all four tips closer to wrist than their MCPs -> cursor inside
`cad` rect -> grab; wrist `(0.55,0.62)->(0.58,0.60)` -> screen
`(1152,799)->(1267,756)` -> `updateElementPosition('cad', +115, -43)`.

## Edge cases & sharp edges

- `numHands: 1` — a second hand is silently ignored; `landmarks[0]` wins.
- Smoothed cursor starts at (0,0) — first frames lerp in from the corner;
  `lastWristPos` only locks on grab so drag doesn't jump.
- Snap scan is O(all interactive DOM nodes) every frame — fine at this scale,
  cache the list if porting to a bigger DOM.
- Fist hit-test uses the *smoothed/snapped* cursor position (finalX/finalY),
  not the wrist — so you aim with the fingertip, then clench.
- Thumb isn't part of the fist check — thumb-out fist still counts (and is
  required for the pinch detector to not conflict).
- `elementFromPoint` ignores `pointer-events-none` layers (cursor, noise,
  backdrop) — by design they can't be clicked or hit-tested.
- No scroll gesture, no right-click, no two-hand gestures, no dwell click.
- Browser/Safari: MediaPipe WASM works but needs a secure context and a user
  gesture for camera permission; iOS standalone-PWA mic issues are
  audio-specific but camera in PWA mode is its own gamble — test early.
- CDN WASM pin (@0.10.0) vs npm dep (0.10.22-rc) mismatch — vendor both for
  a rebuild (same pattern as vendored echarts `/local/` assets on HA hosts).

## Can YOLO do it?

Not directly — wrong-shaped output. YOLO detection gives bounding boxes +
class labels; the ada_v2 UX needs continuous 21-point landmark geometry
(fingertip pointer, sub-pixel pinch distance).

| Requirement | YOLO detection | YOLO-pose (keypoints) |
|---|---|---|
| Fingertip cursor (sub-pixel) | box centre only — too coarse | yes, if trained on hand-keypoint data |
| Pinch distance | not possible | yes |
| Fist/palm classification | yes (train classes, e.g. HaGRID) | derived from keypoints |

### Pros

- **Range/scale** — MediaPipe's palm detector drops hands beyond ~1-2 m; a
  YOLO trained on diverse data detects raised hands across a room (kiosk /
  wall tablet / TV surfaces).
- **Multi-hand/multi-person** tracking is more robust at distance.
- **Vocabulary growth** — new poses = retrain, no hand-tuned landmark
  heuristics (ada_v2's folded-finger check is brittle: ignores thumb, 2-D only).
- Easy server-side GPU inference via ultralytics.

### Cons

- Boxes != landmarks — gesture-class YOLO loses the pointer UX that made it
  feel like Minority Report.
- Custom data/training burden beyond HaGRID's vocabulary.
- Latency — browser WASM/WebGPU MediaPipe runs ~60 fps locally; a server
  round-trip adds 30-100 ms, felt immediately in a pointer UI.
- In-browser YOLO (TFJS/ONNX.js) is heavier than MediaPipe WASM.
- On Pi-class hardware (ada-pi): YOLO won't hit interactive rates on CPU;
  MediaPipe TFLite gets ~15-30 fps on Pi 5, or needs the Hailo AI HAT.

## Recommendation

1. **Keep MediaPipe** if reviving for ada-pi/PWA — or bump to `tasks-vision`
   WebGPU delegate, or `GestureRecognizer` (prebuilt classes: closed fist,
   open palm, point-up, thumbs up/down, victory). The feature was dropped for
   product reasons, not because it failed.
2. **Use YOLO where it wins** — a "hand raised" wake/attention gesture for
   room-scale surfaces. Hybrid: cheap YOLO watch -> activate the landmark
   pipeline only while a hand is up.
3. **Keep the UX layer** — lerp smoothing, snap-with-hysteresis, wrist-delta
   dragging are model-agnostic and made it usable. With YOLO classes add
   N-of-M temporal voting to stop label flicker.
4. **Pi hardware** — prefer inference in the PWA (browser already has webcam +
   GPU) over streaming frames to a GPU server; privacy and latency both better.

Net: YOLO can do gesture *recognition*; ada_v2 was a landmark-driven
*pointer system*. For that, MediaPipe (or any 21-keypoint model) is the
right primitive. YOLO is the answer only if the goal shifts to room-scale,
discrete, multi-person gestures.

## Rebuild checklist (ada-pi / PWA)

1. Vendor `hand_landmarker.task` + tasks-vision WASM locally (no CDN
   dependency; version-lock both to the same release).
2. Port `predictWebcam` verbatim: readyState guard -> canvas draw ->
   (optional) backend frame relay -> landmark pipeline.
3. Port cursor pipeline: flip -> sensitivity -> clamp -> lerp -> snap
   hysteresis -> setCursorPos; DOM cursor div; pinch/fist state machines;
   wrist-delta drag + bounds-by-anchor.
4. Recreate the DOM contract: popup ids, `data-drag-handle`, snap target
   selector, cursor div, Hand toggle button, settings (sensitivity + flip).
5. Decide persistence: ada_v2 kept `camera_flipped` in backend settings.json —
   in ada-pi pick the equivalent (HA input_boolean / PWA localStorage /
   backend settings file).
6. Improve on it: add dwell-click or N-of-M pinch voting, second-hand support
   (`numHands: 2`), `GestureRecognizer` for extra vocabulary, wake-word-style
   "hand up" gate to save GPU when idle.

## References

- Archive report: `docs/kb/archive/ada/ada-v2-platform.md`
- Manifest: `docs/archive/manifests/ada.yml`
- Source: `tonezzz/ada` @ `af6d572` — `ada_v2/src/App.jsx`,
  `ada_v2/src/components/{ToolsModule,SettingsWindow,...}.jsx`,
  `ada_v2/backend/server.py`, `ada_v2/electron/main.js`,
  `ada_v2/hand_gesture_test.py` (standalone OpenCV prototype — wider vocab
  incl. directional pointing + peace sign; scratch code, not shipped),
  `ada_v2/README.md`, `ada_v2/package.json`

# GEV Screen Interaction Benchmark

`gev_screen1_interact` — Ada casts God's Eye View to vcast screen 1 and drives it incrementally. 6 turns: cast → what's showing → fly to Bangkok → zoom to globe → verify view state → stop cast.

## Result

| Run | Expectations | Functional outcome |
|-----|--------------|--------------------|
| run 1 | PASS (0 failed) | cast OK; every `gev_command` hit relay 404 — relay was never deployed |
| run 2 | PASS | `gev_command` called but errored `urllib not defined` — latent bug |
| run 3 | **PASS, functional** | cast → fly Bangkok → zoom globe → state query all delivered to live GEV client |

## Chain verified end-to-end

`Ada tool gev_command` → `POST /apps/gev-cmd/command` → gev-gemini bridge → `function_call` frame → browser clients → `runTool(runner)` executes on the casted page.

## Bugs found & fixed this run

1. **Caddy route missing** — repo `stacks/web/Caddyfile` had `/apps/gev-cmd/*` since commit `472f5a0a` but it was never deployed; running edge had no route (404). Also discovered `/etc/caddy/Caddyfile` had reverted to the stock 13-line template — the entire apps edge was one reload away from total loss; the real config (with gev-cmd) is now on disk and validated on caddy 2.6.2.
2. **Bridge image stale** — deployed `gev-gemini` predated the `/command` endpoint; image rebuilt + restarted.
3. **`gev_command` crash** — `urllib.request` used without import (the import lived inside a sibling method). ada-pi `54ab1c2`.
4. **Passive displays unreachable** — the bridge only counted voice-session sockets as clients; a casted page never registered. **New:** `?remote=1` ws = command-only client, no Gemini Live session (zero quota cost). GEV `index.html` now opens the remote socket at page parse (before Cesium init) and queues commands until the action runner is ready; `gevGeminiRealtime.js` registers a listener after `initGevVoiceCommands`. Live-verified: `/command/health` reports `{clients, remote}`, commands deliver to casted screens.

## Caveats

- **Fire-and-forget**: `/command` returns `delivered` count only — `get_current_view_state` reaches the client but its result doesn't come back through the relay. Verification loop is Ada → relay → screen state, not client-returned state.
- **Broadcast**: commands go to every connected GEV page — if two screens show GEV they both fly.
- **Display must be awake**: iPad suspended = page JS dead = no remote client (screen 1 stayed remote:0 while asleep; screen 2's desktop browser connected instantly).
- Commands on a still-initializing page queue until the action runner exists (early ws + 2s drain).

## Files

- scenario: `ada-pi/tests/scenarios-live/gev_screen1_interact.yaml` (tier: full)
- bridge: `chaba/stacks/tony-dell/gev-gemini/bridge.py` (`REMOTE` set + `?remote=1` path)
- frontend: `gods-eye-view` `index.html` early listener + `src/voice/gevGeminiRealtime.js` `initGevRemoteListener`
- edge: `chaba/stacks/web/Caddyfile` `/apps/gev-cmd/*` → `127.0.0.1:8790` (deployed via admin API + persisted to /etc/caddy)

## Next

- Tool-response return path: bridge waits briefly for remote client's `tool_response` so `get_current_view_state` can answer Ada.
- Screen-scoped commands: `screen=N` arg so broadcast doesn't hit every GEV page.
- iPad wake hook: vcast wakeLock exists but iOS still suspends background tabs.

## Screen narration (added same session)

`vcast_say(screen, text)` — Ada speaks short narration through the display's
own speechSynthesis ("Flying the map to Bangkok"). Implemented:
- vcast `speak` message handler (`stacks/web/public/apps/vcast/index.html`)
- tool `vcast_say` in ada-pi (owner-gated like cast_to_screen; in ACTUATING_TOOLS)
- tool description nudges Ada to announce screen actions inline.
iOS gates speech behind one user tap on the display's "audio" button; before
that the display shows the line as a toast and reports `speak-blocked`.
A sleeping iPad runs no page JS — narration requires the screen awake.

## Verification loop + screen targeting (added 2026-09-29)

The relay is no longer fire-and-forget:
- `POST /command` accepts `{name, args, screen?, wait?}` — `screen:N`
  targets only remotes whose hello announced that vcast screen (the
  same-origin iframe reads `parent.__vcastScreen`; also `?screen=N` url
  param); `wait:>0` collects `tool_response` frames and returns them in
  `responses` — `get_current_view_state` can now actually answer Ada.
- Remote clients announce `{type:'hello', screen}` on ws open (+6s/+20s
  retries — the vcast 'registered' msg races the socket open).
- `/command/health` reports `remote_screens` for debugging.
- Verified end-to-end: hello'd screen-3 python client received a
  screen-scoped command and its tool_response came back in the POST body.
- `gev_command` tool args: `screen` + `wait` (default 3s).

Operational note: displays must be RELOADED to pick up new vcast/GEV
page code — connected screens run whatever JS was loaded at boot
(`{"type":"reload"}` via /pub). Pages still initializing queue commands
until the action runner exists.

## Update — bundle corruption root-caused (2026-09-29)

The 'still initializing' mystery on real browsers was a **corrupted
bundle**: an early path-prefix sed ran unanchored on `dist/` and broke JS
syntax (`Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '/'` — no page JS ran at
all). Fixed: clean `npm run build` + quote-anchored `/api/`/`/models/`
prefixes only; `node --check` gates deploy now. Lesson: never regex-patch
minified bundles without a syntax check.

Also verified live:
- `uplink_confirm_flow` scenario — full PASS (confirm-gate before camera
  uplink, acknowledge running capture, clean stop, lease cleared)
- `cast_switch_flow` scenario — full PASS (confirm gates, source switch,
  busy-destination check, move, teardown). Notably strict consent:
  'screen 4 is free' was NOT accepted as camera permission — she asked
  again explicitly.

## gev_screen4_interact — FULL PASS (2026-09-29)

All 7 turns green on a live browser display: cast → confirm → describe →
fly Bangkok → zoom globe → verify (real view-state returned in
`responses` — Ada honestly reported ~18,000km near Austin, i.e. drifted
from Bangkok after zoom-out) → stop.

Two bugs this run flushed out:

1. **Cross-session speaker bleed** — a concurrent `simulate_speaker=KK`
   scenario flipped the shared runner's `current_speaker_ha_person` and
   MY session's cast/gev calls were denied as `person.kk` (owner-gated).
   Fixed: `execute()` takes `speaker=` via `_CALLER_SPEAKER` contextvar;
   explicit None (unidentified session) no longer falls back to the
   shared field. ada-pi `012dee9` + `e73a15f`, 58 unit tests green.
2. **Phantom assertion keys** — `result_contains_any` and quoted
   substrings (`"ok": true`) silently no-op'd/missed because tool results
   arrive JSON-escaped in events. Assertions rewritten escape-agnostic
   (`delivered`, `responses` bare; both `": 0` serializations blocked).

# God's Eye View — development jobs & Ada control plan

Platform: Cesium geospatial app (`gods-eye-view`), own voice bridge
`gev-gemini` (Gemini Live, :8789 on tony-dell), ~28 frontend tools
(camera, layers, tracking, CCTV, annotations, analyst queries).

## Goal

Cast GEV to the TV via vcast → talk to Ada → Ada drives the casted GEV
client ("fly to London", "show flights", "track that plane") while the
TV shows the result. Ada replaces GEV's own voice AI when casted.

## Cast audit (chrome-devtools, 2026-09-27)

Verified live with a headless Chrome receiver (`?room=vcast-9`):

- `POST /pub {room, msg:{type:"nav"}}` → delivered in **~183ms**
- `https://tony-dell…/apps/gev/` **renders inside the vcast iframe** —
  globe, imagery tiles, terrain all load; title "God's Eye View"
- only noise: 2×404 on `/api/google/nearby-places` (not proxied —
  non-blocking), `/apps/gev/api/setup/status` pends (bridge healthcheck)
- input-bridge relay healthy via Caddy; 2 stale screens
  (screen-2 headless-test, screen-3 gate-test) disconnected — can release
- UX gap found: a fresh device lands in `pending` forever until an
  admin `/claim` — Ada should claim/assign when asked to cast to a
  new screen

## Development jobs

| # | job | status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `POST /command` on gev-gemini bridge → forwards function_call frames to connected GEV clients | **dispatched** (omen lane, 2026-09-27 ~14:12) |
| 2 | Ada `gev_*` tool family (bounded subset: fly_to_location, zoom, layers, track_entity, analyst_query) | pending (after #1) |
| 3 | `gev_cast` scenario: vcast /apps/gev/ → TV client registers → Ada drives | pending |
| 4 | vcast smoothness audit — relay OK; needs a connected TV receiver for end-to-end | in progress |
| 5 | CMS UX: mobile collapse + filter + active-page highlight | **done** (`7aeb163`, `f38e29e`) |
| 6 | Benchmarks: pub→render latency ~183ms (relay) + Cesium ~5-10s first-globe | measured |

## Notes

- Command endpoint must address a specific client when several GEV tabs
  are open (client id or 'most recent').
- Keep GEV's own mic off on casted sessions — Ada is the voice layer.

# Hosting Provider Assessment

_2026-09-27 · Devin · idc02 spec: Linux · ≥4 vCPU · ≥16GB RAM · ≥200GB SSD · daily backups · ~฿800/mo_

## Shortlist

| Provider / Plan | vCPU | RAM | SSD | Price/mo | DC | Meets spec? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ReadyIDC VPS Business L2SS** | 4 | 16 GB | 300 GB | ฿800 (+7% VAT = ฿856) | Thailand | ✅ exact fit, at budget |
| **ReadyIDC VPS Game LG2SS+** | 8 | 18 GB | 150 GB | ฿800 | Thailand | ⚠️ storage short 50GB |
| ReadyIDC VPS Game LG3SS+ | 10 | 26 GB | 200 GB | ฿1,100 | Thailand | ✅ over budget 37% |
| **Contabo Cloud VPS 8** | 8 | 24 GB | 300 GB | €11.20 (~฿420, 24-mo price; €14 list) | **Singapore** | ✅ 2× spec at half price |
| Hetzner CPX41 | 8 | 16 GB | 240 GB NVMe | €23.29 (~฿880) + backups ~20% → ~฿1,050 | EU (SIN ~$39 = ฿1,370) | ✅ over budget ~30% |
| _reference: Siamdata (idc01)_ | — | — | — | ฿800-ish | Thailand | existing provider |

## Caveats that decide this

**Backups are not free anywhere.** None of the plans include daily
backups by default — Hetzner auto-backup is +20%, Contabo gives 3
snapshots (manual), ReadyIDC sells backup as a separate product line.
The spec's "daily backups included" effectively means *self-managed
backup* (our mddb-backup.timer pattern) regardless of provider — do
not pay extra for it unless it's a real managed service.

**Contabo's price is real but so is its reputation**: oversubscribed
hosts, CPU steal at peak hours, ticket support measured in days. For
mddb's sustained-index-rebuild workload — exactly what saturated idc01 —
Contabo is a coin flip. Fine for Chaba Lab; risky for production mddb.

**Latency**: Thai DC ~1–5ms from home; Singapore ~10–30ms; EU ~180ms.
For an Ada-facing node, SIN is acceptable, EU is not for interactive
paths (but fine for batch memory/index workloads).

**Provider-correlation risk still stands**: a second Siamdata box shares
the failure modes of idc01. ReadyIDC is a different Thai operator —
same latency, different blast radius. That argues *for* ReadyIDC over
a second Siamdata.

## Recommendation

1. **ReadyIDC VPS Business L2SS (฿856 incl. VAT)** — meets the spec
   *exactly* at budget, Thai DC (voice-adjacent latency), independent
   provider (no correlation with Siamdata), Thai support. The
   straightforward idc02 pick.
2. **Contabo Cloud VPS 8 (~฿420)** — if the node is for Lab/bench
   workloads where occasional CPU-steal hurts nothing. Twice the spec
   at half the price; just don't put production mddb there without a
   soak test.
3. **Hetzner CPX41 (~฿1,050 w/ backups)** — if quality/API maturity
   beats budget. Over budget but the cleanest ops story (Terraform,
   hourly billing, snapshot API). EU latency fine for batch, not for
   Ada-facing services.

**Public IP optional**: with the Cloudflare Tunnel edge (see
`chaba-edge-plan`), idc02 does not need its own public IPv4 — outbound
cloudflared covers "public" reach, and tailnet covers admin. That
removes the included-IP line from the decision and slightly favors
the cheapest spec-fit (Contabo) — though ReadyIDC remains the pick for
provider independence + Thai latency.

**Keep the original split either way**: mddb/indexing on idc02, Ada +
edge stays on idc01, tailnet-only, replicate-then-cutover.

# IDC02 Proposal — offload node for idc01

_2026-09-27 · Devin · measured on idc01 live (podman stats + service RSS)_

## Why

idc01 (Siamdata VPS, 2 vCPU / 12 GB / 100 GB) is saturated. Steady-state
usage is ~10 of 12 GB, and mddb alone consumes ~8.6 GB — enough that it
was in a cgroup-OOM crash loop today until its bounds were raised. Every
mddb restart wedges Ada's memory backend for minutes, and there is no
headroom left for Chaba Lab or any new workload.

## Current footprint (measured)

| Service | RSS (steady) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| mddb | **~8.6 GB** (rebuild spikes to ceiling) | memory/vector DB — the hog |
| ada-ha-tony | ~350 MB | production voice (latency-sensitive) |
| ada-ha-michael | ~110 MB | production voice |
| ada-pi-pwa | ~65 MB | PWA backend |
| open-notebook + surreal | ~340 MB | notebook stack |
| obsidian-vault | ~100 MB | vault sync target |
| ollama | ~10 MB idle / ~2 GB loaded | embed fallback (now unused — OR-only) + lab models |
| edge + proxy + panel + misc | <150 MB total | Caddy :80/:443 public edge, embed proxy |

## Proposed split

**idc01 keeps** (latency-critical / edge / small):
- Caddy public edge (:80/:443), input-bridge
- ada-ha-tony, ada-ha-michael, ada-pi-pwa (voice paths stay near the edge)
- obsidian-vault, gemini-ollama-proxy, mddb-panel

**idc02 gets** (memory-heavy / stateful / bursty):
- **mddb primary** (~9 GB working set, needs room to grow)
- open-notebook + surreal
- ollama (dev/lab models; embedding no longer needed — OR is primary)
- Chaba Lab when it deploys (was never viable on idc01 anyway)

tony-dell already runs an mddb binlog follower — with idc02 as primary
the replication topology stays intact and DR improves.

## Suggested spec (same provider — Siamdata)

**Recommended: 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 150 GB**

- 16 GB: mddb (9–10) + notebook (~0.4) + ollama (~2–4 loaded) + lab (~3)
  still leaves headroom; a 12 GB box would already be tight on day one.
- 4 vCPU: mddb's cold-start index build is CPU-bound — on 2 vCPU today it
  churned ~10 min per restart and starved all HTTP requests. 4 cores
  roughly halves that pain and gives the lab room to breathe.
- 150 GB: mddb.db + vectors grow; lab adds images/models.

**Cheaper floor: 2 vCPU / 16 GB / 100 GB** — works if the lab goes
elsewhere later; vCPU is the part that hurts least to start with on
Siamdata since upgrades are resize-reboots.

## Pros

- idc01 drops to ~2 GB used — ada voice + edge get a quiet, stable host;
  today's wedge-class incident disappears
- mddb gets real headroom + faster rebuilds; Ada memory ops stop being
  the failure-blast-radius of every restart
- Chaba Lab finally has a home without touching prod
- Same provider = same DC latency (~1 ms tailnet RTT) — mddb→ada calls
  add no meaningful delay

## Cons

- New monthly cost (est. Siamdata 4c/16G tier — check panel pricing)
- Second public IP = second thing to secure/patch; Caddy edge stays on
  idc01 so idc02 can be tailnet-only (recommended — don't expose it)
- Provider-correlated failure: one DC outage takes both (mitigated —
  tony-dell keeps an mddb replica)
- One-time migration: mddb.db + HNSW indexes move with ~30–60 min
  downtime, or replication-promote cutover (cleaner — seed replica on
  idc02, then promote)

## Suggestion

1. Order 4 vCPU / 16 GB / 150 GB on Siamdata, tailnet-only.
2. Bring up mddb as a replication follower first, verify, then promote —
  avoids a dump/restore window.
3. Move open-notebook + ollama after mddb is proven stable on idc02.
4. Keep Chaba Lab quota-capped there; re-evaluate idc01 sizing after a
  month — it may be worth downsizing to 8 GB once mddb is gone.

# Jev AI Assessment — v2 (measured)

_2026-09-28 · Devin · reconciles pilot + model bench + Ada/GEV/Weaviate plan_

## Verdict

Jev (decision-only models, `/v1/systemone`) earns a permanent seat in the
stack — as an **async judgment tier now**, a **hot-path gate tier later**.
Local open-jev is live on tony-omen `:8777` (gemma-3-4b-it, CPU).

## Measured (3-backend bench, 18 real Ada decisions)

| backend | accuracy | latency | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| open-jev gemma-3-4b (CPU) | **83%** | 11.9s | calibrated — honest 0.559 on ambiguous turns |
| open-jev gemma-3-1b | 56% | 2.6s | too weak — under-scores plain "yes" |
| Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenRouter | 57% | 1.4s | **uncalibrated — worse than the regex; do NOT gate through chat models** |

The `/v1/systemone` wire contract is backend-portable; the value is
logit-read scores. Chat models self-report confidence — structurally
fake calibration.

## Decision tier ladder

```
Tier 0  RULES      μs         gates, budgets, whitelists
Tier 1a JEV-async  ~12s CPU   post-turn audit, scenario judging, CMS classification  ← NOW
Tier 1b JEV-hot    ~400ms     confirm-gate, tool routing, ambient filtering          ← needs quant/NanoJev/hosted
Tier 2  GEMINI     streams    reasoning, generation, correction duty
```

Rule: cheapest tier that can hold the decision reliably. Each Jev win
removes a Gemini round-trip AND a failure surface.

## Ada↔GEV topology (as built)

- **Ada → `gev_command`** → `POST /command` (:8790) → function_call →
  GEV browsers — inherits Ada's full enforcement stack.
- **GEV's own Gemini session** in the bridge → 28 tools, **no confirm
  gate/budget/ops events** — the unguarded actuation path.
- Fix: thin guard shim in `gev-gemini/bridge.py` (budget + confirm +
  ops events) before any shared-gateway refactor.

## Data plane (unchanged)

MDDB canonical for Ada banks (Gemini-768 space, OR-Vertex primary —
cosine 1.000 proven). Weaviate stays dev-KB hybrid search (MiniLM
space). Different vector spaces — never merge; scope grows only via
retrieval bench data.

## Sequence

1. jev-bench committed → `tests/bench/jev-bench.py` emits
   `kind: benchmark` docs → auto-report catches regressions
2. Async Jev first: post-turn confirm audit, scenario judging
3. gev bridge guard shim (budget + confirm + ops events)
4. Retrieval bench: MDDB-vs-Weaviate recall@5 + latency
5. Hot-path Jev decision with bench numbers: 4-bit quant on the 1650 /
   NanoJev-0.6B trained on our transcripts / hosted API

Full reasoning + ecosystem scan: kb-system
`jev-weaviate-architecture-assessment.md`.

# LINE Bot — outbound messaging project

Date: 2026-09-27 · consolidated for review

## What it is

Outbound LINE notifications — system → Tony (alerts, dispatches,
Ada-initiated messages). Distinct from **Yomi**, which *reads* LINE.

## Current state — gaps found 2026-09-27

- **No Ada tool exists to send LINE messages.** When Tony asked
  "send me a test message" (session 7975f60c71, ~11:15), Ada could only
  call `ada_memory_search` + `web_search` — she guessed and checked the
  LINE Bot *API status page* instead of sending. Nothing arrived.
- **No LINE Messaging-API channel token** found in secrets on idc01 or
  on this box — the classic "bot account + push API" path isn't wired.
- The only working send path is **Yomi's `send_message`** (E2EE send as
  Tony's own account to any chatId) — but that MCP server is not
  reachable from Ada's tool layer, and its session is revoked (see the
  Line Yomi page).

## Proposed path

1. Re-login Yomi (passwordless secondary-device flow on Tony's phone —
   `login` → PIN → `login_complete`; ~3 min window).
2. Expose a thin `line_send` Ada tool: `tool_runner` → yomi
   `send_message` (a small HTTP shim or a local CLI wrapper on idc01).
   Tools needed: `line_send(to, text)` + `line_chats()` for resolving
   recipients. Gate under `ADA_DEV_TOOLS`-style confirmed writes —
   outbound messages are consequential.
3. Until wired, Ada's honest answer is: "LINE send is offline — needs
   Tony's re-login." (Memory note `yomi-vs-line-bot` updated with this.)

## Pending

- [ ] Tony: LINE re-login on the phone (allow-from-other-devices + PIN)
- [ ] Devin: `line_send`/`line_chats` Ada tools via yomi
- [ ] Optional later: dedicated LINE Messaging-API bot channel (cleaner
      identity — messages come *from Ada*, not "from Tony")

# Yomi — LINE archive, search & send

Date: 2026-09-27 · consolidated for review

## What it is

LINE message **archive + search + E2EE send** running as the `yomi` MCP
server. Pulls chats via LINE's secondary-device protocol, decrypts E2EE,
summarizes into MDDB, exposes MCP tools. See chaba-docs
`architecture/yomi-architecture-separation.md` (fetch vs process split).

## Capabilities (MCP tools)

- `list_conversations`, `get_chat_messages`, `get_unread_digest`,
  `get_insight` — read/search
- `get_message_media` — decrypted images/video/audio
- **`send_message`** — real E2EE outbound to any chatId (already works —
  the only live LINE-send path in the stack)
- `login`/`login_complete` — passwordless re-auth on Tony's phone

## Status — OFFLINE as of 2026-09-27

`list_conversations` → `Access token refresh required`. Session revoked
(typically when LINE on the phone re-logs elsewhere). Digest→MDDB and
any send path are both blocked until re-login.

**Re-login flow** (Tony, ~3 min): enable 允許自其他裝置登入 on the phone
→ `login` (phone/region) → LINE shows a PIN → `login_complete`
immediately → device approved on the phone.

## Indexed data

- ~489 daily digests in MDDB (`ada-ha-bank-yomi` family)
- Searchable via `ada_memory_search` (bank='yomi') and the MCP tools
- Privacy default: capture-all; excluded chats via `exclude_chats`

## Confusion note for Ada

Yomi ≠ LINE bot. Yomi **reads** (and can send as Tony's account); the
"LINE bot" concept is outbound notifications — currently unbuilt on the
Ada side. See `line-bot` report.

# Memory audit — KK misses, confident-gate incident, scenario assessment

Date: 2026-09-27 · incidents from live sessions + scenario runs

## Why Ada misses KK's memory — root cause chain

1. **Extraction lands in Tony's bank.** `speaker_identity` routes
   extracts to `personal-kk` only when speaker-ID resolves KK. Since
   2026-09-24 her sessions resolve to admin/Tony (mis-identified or
   unidentified → caller identity) → extracts land in
   `ada-ha-bank-personal-tony` (daily) while `personal-kk` froze at
   9-24. Then ACL (`person.kk` allow-list) blocks her from reading where
   her own data went.
2. **Wiped docs poisoned ranking** (fixed today `6745f31`): 3 of 10
   personal-kk docs had contentMd='' yet scored ~0.6 — they crowded the
   real hits out. Now: empty hits skipped, meta-only writes refuse when
   the read fails, dead docs retracted.
3. **Profile contamination** (`Timmy`, `NewSpeaker`) still muddies
   speaker-ID → feeds issue 1. Awaiting approval to remove + re-enroll.

Evidence: KK=กุ้ง=Sok Hiang merge note + "CR-V ขาว 5ขว 6249" +
Underworld/EDM + แก้วตา assistant-name all found inside
`ada-ha-bank-personal-tony` extracts 2026-09-26.

## The confident-gate incident — explained

Ada refused "dig deeper" (`recall_gate_override` reproduces it):
server-side `_recall_gated` refuses `ada_session_recall` for 60s after a
confident memory_search hit (score≥0.6). Rationale is sound — saves the
~20s NotebookLM round-trip — but the gate trusted hits whose bodies
were empty, and gave the user no override path.

**Balance now in place** (`d96cf88`):
- Gate only counts confident *content-bearing* hits (empty hits gone)
- `force=true` escapes the gate on explicit push ("dig deeper", "check
  again", "you missed it") — verified live: turn 2 reached recall
- Instruction names the override so she doesn't second-guess it

## References lifecycle — tested (`report_references_lifecycle`, PASS)

Create-with-references → publish → "remove references" → update →
re-read. Workflow valid; found and fixed a real regex bug along the way:
`confirmed?` never matched bare "confirm" (`10f0211`).

## Scenario structure — assessment

**Pros**
- Declarative YAML, one file per capability — easy to add
- `calls_any`/`no_calls_except`/`response_nonempty`/`reconnect` cover
  the real axes; `cleanup.mddb_delete` keeps banks clean
- Live traces caught 4 real bugs today (regex, sticky identity, dead
  stream, wiped docs)

**Cons**
- English expectations vs Thai answers — can't assert on response
  content (`response_contains` only works same-language)
- No speaker-ID injection — can't simulate "talking as KK" so
  per-person memory routing is untestable end-to-end
- `calls_any` silently passes if the runner's tool-name list drifts
  from reality (add a `known_tools` check against the declaration set)
- No per-turn assertions on *args* (e.g. `provider=duckduckgo` asserted
  only via journal grep, not the scenario)

**Suggested improvements**
- `response_regex` + `response_lang` assertions (transcript is captured
  already)
- `speaker:` per-session field → `?speaker_override=person.kk` query
  param honored by the session path, so KK-scoped flows are testable
- A `--dry-run known_tools` lint: every `calls_any` name must exist in
  the declared tool set
- Coverage matrix job (running on mn01) → auto-flag uncovered tools

# Analysis: Migrating Home Assistant and Ada Public URLs to idc01

This document outlines the pros and cons of moving the public entry points for Home Assistant and Ada from their current location on `mn01` to `idc01` (Siamdata VPS, tailnet node 100.74.146.0).

## Current Architecture
- Ada is public via `mn01` Tailscale Funnel.
- `tony-ha` is tailnet-only.
- `idc01` has tailscale serve on tailnet only, no funnel enabled.

## Pros

*   **Consolidation:** Moves public-facing component to a dedicated, public-facing VPS (`idc01` has a static public IP), potentially simplifying network management and decoupling public access from internal node `mn01`.
*   **Availability:** VPS generally has higher availability and more reliable direct network access than a residential connection subject to ISP whims.

## Cons

*   **Increased Latency:** Moving the entry point to `idc01` introduces an additional network hop for the voice websocket (User -> `idc01` -> tailnet to `mn01`). This likely increases voice response latency.
*   **Origin Change:** A new public URL means the browser context (origin) changes. This will **invalidate device-bound API keys** stored in browser `localStorage` and will require re-installation of installed PWAs.
*   **Migration Effort:** Requires configuring `tailscale serve`/`funnel` on `idc01`, updating DNS, updating Ada's configuration, and migrating user data across all devices.
*   **Security Exposure:** Enabling public ingress on `idc01` presents fresh attack surface to the internet.

## Recommendation

Due to the increased voice latency and the breaking changes for users (PWA reinstall, API key invalidation), **migration is not recommended** at this time unless direct `mn01` ingress becomes untenable, or if `idc01` provides tangible performance gains outweighing the extra hop. The current configuration on `mn01` via Tailscale Funnel appears optimal for balancing security, latency, and operational simplicity.

# Monitoring Proposal — multi-host dashboard

_2026-09-27 · Devin · researched: github candidates vs our actual estate_

## Requirement

One dashboard showing load/health across all hosts and services —
idc01, tony-dell, tony-omen, mn01 (+ michael-ha where possible).
Constraints that shape the answer: everything is **rootless podman
quadlets** (no docker), hosts are **tailnet-only**, and idc01 is a
12 GB VPS that can't afford a heavy monitoring stack on top of mddb.

## Candidates evaluated

### 1. Beszel — github.com/henrygd/beszel ⭐ recommended

Hub + agent model: lightweight Go hub (PocketBase, ~50 MB) + tiny agent
per host. Single pane: CPU/mem/disk/net per host + per-container stats.

- **Podman: works** — agent reads podman socket via `DOCKER_HOST=
  unix:///run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock` (Docker-compat API).
- Best run as a **systemd binary agent** (not container): rootless
  agents can't see systemd services/temps/GPU otherwise.
- Alerts (threshold → email/webhook), Docker **and** podman container
  lists with cpu/mem.
- Known quirks: container CPU% inflated ~3.5× for containers inside
  pods (issue #1953); `-infra` pod containers can't be excluded yet;
  container health doesn't show for podman (#1298).

**Fit: best** — smallest footprint, single dashboard for "what's going
on everywhere", exactly the "sense of the estate" need.

### 2. Netdata — github.com/netdata/netdata

Per-host agent, zero-config beautiful dashboards, discovers podman
containers via cgroups automatically, systemd units visible, and
parent/child streaming gives one entry point. Deepest metrics
(processes, cgroup internals, eBPF).

- Cons: heavier agent (~150–300 MB RAM each), busy UI, long-term
  retention via cloud account (free tier exists but pushes Netdata
  Cloud).
- **Fit: strong #2** — best if we want deep per-host forensics
  (e.g. today's mddb wedge would've been instantly diagnosable).

### 3. Prometheus + Grafana + exporters — the "grown-up" stack

- `containers/prometheus-podman-exporter` (official containers org,
  active, podman v5) + `node_exporter` per host → Prometheus → Grafana.
- Pros: max flexibility, proper alertmanager, retention control;
  mddb already exposes `/metrics` — could scrape it directly.
- Cons: **most moving parts** — prometheus server, dashboards to build,
  3-4 exporters × 4 hosts; overkill for "what's going on" and it lands
  on the host we need to watch most.
- **Fit: only if we later need alerting/retention pipelines.**

### Rejected

- **Dozzle** — container logs only, no metrics.
- **Uptime Kuma** — availability checks; we already have mcp-health.
- **Glances** — great per-host TUI/web, no real multi-host aggregation.
- **Zabbix/cAdvisor** — enterprise weight / docker-only.

## Proposal

**Beszel hub on tony-dell** (always-on, tailnet, lightest VPS) —
agents on idc01, tony-omen, mn01, tony-dell. michael-ha can't run an
agent (HAOS appliance) — its health stays in HA + mcp-health instead.

```
tony-dell  beszel-hub :8090 (tailnet only)
    ↑ TCP 45876
idc01      beszel-agent (systemd unit, DOCKER_HOST=podman.sock)
tony-omen  beszel-agent (idem — sees GPU? via binary agent)
mn01       beszel-agent (idem)
tony-dell  beszel-agent (idem)
```

Effort: ~30 min — hub container/quadlet + 4 binary agents + one
`podman.socket` enable per host. Cost: ~50 MB hub + ~20 MB/agent RAM.

Optional phase 2: Netdata on idc01 only (the host that keeps hurting),
pointed at nothing — its per-host dashboard is standalone.

## Why not just scrape with Grafana?

Today the failure mode we actually fight is "host quietly saturated"
(mddb 8.6 GB OOM loop). Beszel shows that instantly with zero build
work. If we later need per-metric alerting or long retention, the
Prometheus path composes on top — nothing about Beszel blocks it.

# สมุดคำศัพท์ของ Tony

Tony's word list — terms that came up in sessions, in plain words.

Two sources keep this page:
- **Ada** logs a term quietly when she recasts one mid-conversation (vocab_note → tony's personal bank), then syncs here.
- **Devin** adds terms from Devin sessions directly.

## From Devin — cleanup words (2026-09-27)

**audit** — look and count only. Measures and reports, touches nothing.

**prune** — delete old copies, keep the newest.

**consolidate** — merge duplicates into one.

**retention** — a standing rule that auto-deletes after X days. For logs, not memories.

**methodology** — the ordered way of doing a thing: the steps and the reason for their order.

**bloat** — data growing faster than it is useful.

## From Devin — memory words

**embedding** — turning text into a number-list (vector) so search can match by meaning, not just exact words.

**quantization (int8)** — shrinking those number-lists 4x smaller with almost no quality loss.

**HNSW index** — the fast "meaning lookup" structure. Loading it into RAM is what ate the memory.

**cursor** — a bookmark of "how far did we ship" so a sync resumes where it stopped.

**provenance** — a stamp recording which model made an embedding; if the model changes, old embeddings need redoing.

**prune** — ลบสำเนาเก่า เก็บแค่ตัวล่าสุด

**consolidate** — รวมของที่ซ้ำกันให้เหลือชิ้นเดียว

# Neuralink Project Deep Research Report

## Executive Summary

Neuralink, founded in 2016 by Elon Musk, is developing implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). The company hit a major milestone in January 2024 with its first successful human implant in patient Noland Arbaugh. Despite controversies regarding animal testing and transparency, the FDA cleared further human trials, and Neuralink is advancing its goal of creating a next-generation device with significantly higher connection capacity than current approved BCIs. Key competitors include Synchron, Precision Neuroscience, and Blackrock Neurotech.

## Key Findings

### History & Mission
Launched publicly in 2017, Neuralink aims to build a BCI with over 100 times more brain connections than FDA-approved competitors.

### Milestones & Human Trials
- **Jan 2024:** First human implant.
- **2024:** Successful demonstrations by patient Noland Arbaugh.

### Competitors & Criticism
While under scrutiny for ethical and developmental protocols, Neuralink continues to address concerns publicly. Major competition comes from established players like Synchron (stent-based BCI) and Blackrock Neurotech, and newer firms like Precision Neuroscience.

# NEWS Source Assessment — awesome-ai-news

*Assessed 2026-09-27 · repo: github.com/taielab/awesome-ai-news (55★, curated list of AI news/RSS aggregation tools)*

## What the list offers

Curated catalog across 10 categories: news aggregation, RSS processing, academic tracking, GitHub trending, social monitoring, podcast generation, message distribution, security news, static-site publishing.

## Fit to our stack (Ada + news-* CMS pages + chaba digests)

### High value — adopt patterns now

| Repo | Why it fits |
|---|---|
| **ai-news-radar** | 10+ source list with **failed-source handling** + OPML export — its source table is a ready-made seed for our news-* pages |
| **RSS-Master** | AI summarization + **scoring/dedup** of feeds — exactly the step our news pages lack (pages are Ada-written, no feed pipeline) |
| **clawfeed** | Multi-frequency digests (4h/daily/weekly) — mirrors our L1/L2 memory model; good template for a `news-daily` refresh cadence |
| **ai-trend-publish** | Multi-source → published page pipeline — same shape as our `cms_publish_page` + scenario flow, useful conventions to borrow |

### Structural fix — removes the web_search dependency

Our news flow currently leans on `web_search`, which **hit its quota** in the hosting-assessment run. An RSS-based ingestion removes that dependency entirely:

| Option | Shape | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **FreshRSS** (self-host) | Canonical feed hub on tony-dell/idc02; Ada queries dedup'd items instead of searching | container + reader API |
| **FeedCraft** (Go) | HTML→RSS for sites with no feed (readyidc changelog, Thai gov/news pages) + AI prompts on feeds | single binary, cron |
| **RSS-Master** pattern | scoring + dedup + summaries into MDDB; news-* pages render from there | code, no new service |

Recommended path: **FeedCraft or direct feeds → MDDB doc per item → cms pages render from MDDB.** No new infra in v1; FreshRSS later if the volume justifies a reader.

### Distribution ideas (later)

- **TrendRadar-style** unified timeline + push channels → maps to our chaba-admin events / iPhone notifications, or LINE via yomi.
- **PodRSS / rss_ai_podcast** — RSS→audio brief; Ada already has TTS paths, so a spoken daily brief is feasible once the digest exists.
- **secfeed** — real-time security feed if we want a `news-security` page.

## Recommendations (ordered)

1. Seed the news-* sources table from ai-news-radar's curated list (tagged, with per-source health tracking — it handles failures explicitly).
2. Add an RSS ingestion job (FeedCraft or plain feedparser) writing scored/deduped items to MDDB — kills the web_search quota dependency.
3. Give news-* pages a cadence: clawfeed-style (4h/daily/weekly sections) via the existing scenario runner timer.
4. Later: push distribution (LINE via yomi / chaba-admin) + optional audio brief via Ada TTS.

## Not adopted

- **TelegramForwarder / RSS-to-Telegram-Bot** — Telegram-specific; we push to LINE/iPhone.
- **x-kit / social scrapers** — auth-heavy, brittle; low value per effort for our use.
- Static-site generators (Hextra) — we already have the miniapp/CMS rendering path.

# News System

The `news-*` pages are Ada-maintained daily briefs. Grouped by slug prefix —
filter the page list by "news" or use the links below.

## Pages
- [News Headline](#/news-headline) — combined TL;DR, skim-first
- [News World](#/news-world)
- [News Thailand](#/news-thailand)
- [News Bangplee](#/news-bangplee)
- [News Tabsai](#/news-tabsai) — Bangsaen & Bangphra
- [News Flood](#/news-flood) — automated Thai flood feed

## Required structure — every news-* page MUST have ALL of these

The CMS audit fails any page missing one. Do not publish without them.

1. **H1** — `# <Title>` as the first line, matching the page title.
2. **TL;DR** — `TL;DR:` one sentence, concrete, no adjectives.
3. **3–5 items**, most actionable first. Each item:
   - headline ≤90 chars
   - 1–2 sentence summary
   - `Why it matters:` one concrete sentence
   - `[Source](url)` link to the article/site it came from
4. **Footer** — `*Updated HH:MM ICT*` at the bottom.

If a scope has no real news (e.g. Tasai), say so in the TL;DR and keep
only items actually relevant to that scope — do not pad with national
news that belongs on news-thailand.

## Update flow
1. `web_search` per scope (duckduckgo default, gemini fallback).
2. Draft in the format above → `cms_publish_page` (registers pending).
3. User confirms → resubmit with `confirmed=true`, then `cms_verify_page`.
4. Scenario `news-pages-update` in `tests/scenarios-live/` exercises this.

ควรทานแต่พอดี ประมาณ **หนึ่งกำมือต่อวัน** การรับประทานมากเกินไปอาจทำให้เกิดผลข้างเคียงได้ เช่น ท้องอืด ท้องผูก หรือท้องเสีย เนื่องจากถั่วมีกากใยและไขมันเยอะ

## กินถั่วกับนมได้ไหม?

**กินได้ครับ** โดยทั่วไปไม่เป็นอันตรายอะไร แถมยังได้รับสารอาหารที่หลากหลายทั้งจากถั่วและนมด้วย แต่บางคนอาจจะมีอาการท้องอืด หรือไม่สบายท้องได้ ถ้ามีปัญหาเรื่องการย่อยนมหรือถั่วครับ

# open-jev backend benchmark — Verdict-151M vs gemma-3-4b

**Date:** 2026-09-29
**Host:** tony-omen (i7-9750H 6c/12t, 32 GiB RAM, GTX 1650 4 GB)
**Question:** can Ada's `/v1/systemone` decision service stop burning 15.5 GiB RSS + ~400% CPU on omen?

## TL;DR

| Backend | Latency | Memory | Real-corpus accuracy (confirm-gate noul, n=31) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-3-4b, torch CPU (live :8777) | 10–70 s | 15.5 GiB RSS | **31/31 vs regex** (calibrated: pos 0.999, neg 0.015) |
| gemma-3-1b, torch CUDA | ~0.28 s | ~2 GiB + 2.3 GiB VRAM | not evaluated on corpus; 0/3 agreement on HA probes |
| gemma-3-1b, torch CPU | ~3–9 s | ~5 GiB | same as 1b-CUDA |
| gemma-3-4b, CUDA | — | OOM (needs ~8.6 GiB fp16, card has 3.63 GiB) | — |
| **Verdict-151M (GLiClass/ModernBERT), CPU** | **~90–250 ms** | **~950 MiB, no GPU** | **10/31 single-label, 8/12 multi-label subset — fails zero-shot** |

## What was tested

1. `/score` option-scoring on 5 hand-written HA routing probes → Verdict looked perfect (5/5), 1b was wrong (0/3 vs 4b).
2. **Real corpus replay**: `~/.local/share/ada/jev-corpus.jsonl` on idc01 (31 rows captured by Ada's `jev_confirm_probe` — real user turns with regex labels + recorded 4b scores). Replayed verbatim through a wire-compatible Verdict shim on `127.0.0.1:8778`.

## Results on real data (the part that matters)

The real workload is **noul confirm-gate detection**: "the user turn was 'X' — did they affirm?" 

- **4b: essentially perfect.** Positives ~0.999, negatives ~0.015. Genuinely good at this task.
- **Verdict single-label softmax: no class separation at all** — pos mean 0.938, neg mean 0.916. Two-way softmax saturates when both hypotheses are weak.
- **Verdict multi-label (independent sigmoids): real signal, threshold-sensitive** — positives ~0.995; negatives spread 0.3–0.8. 8/12 on subset at P≥0.5.
- **1b (both devices): wrong picks on HA probes** — e.g. "turn off kitchen lights" for a dim-to-warm request.

## Conclusions

1. **Zero-shot model swaps are dead ends.** 4b's quality on this exact task is unusually good; every cheaper off-the-shelf option measurably degrades it. The earlier "Verdict will just work" hypothesis was wrong — synthetic probes overestimated it.
2. **The designed path is distillation, and the data already exists.** `jev-corpus.jsonl` is explicitly the "training data for a distilled confirm-gate student" (realtime_provider.py). 31 rows now, growing with every confirm-gate event. The 4b is effectively an expensive teacher labeling a corpus at ~12 s/row.
3. **The 4b's cost is partially self-inflicted.** It's advisory-only (regex enforces; Jev measures divergence + captures labels). We're paying ~400% CPU + 15.5 GiB for corpus labels, not for decisions.

## Options going forward

| Option | Cost | Expected outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Fine-tune Verdict/ModernBERT on jev-corpus + 4b-distilled augmentation | ~1 session + corpus growth | ~150M CPU model, <100 ms, task-calibrated. The intended endgame. |
| Tiny classifier on MiniLM embeddings (mn01:5000 already serves them) | logistic-reg on embeddings, ~1 file | cheapest student; needs the corpus to grow first (~200+ rows) |
| jevlike head on gemma-3-1b features | works on CUDA already | middle path; still needs labels |
| Keep 4b CPU but cap it (`CPUQuota=`, fewer threads) | 0 code | kills 10–70 s tail under contention; keeps corpus flowing |
| Retire the probe entirely | 0 | frees all resources; loses corpus + divergence signal |

## Artifacts

- Verdict shim (Jev-compatible, multi-label-capable): `tony-omen:/tmp/verdict_serve.py` (running on `127.0.0.1:8778`, ephemeral)
- Corpus replay scripts: `tony-omen:/tmp/replay_corpus.py`, `/tmp/replay_multi.py`; results `/tmp/corpus-ab.json`
- Corpus source: `idc01:~/.local/share/ada/jev-corpus.jsonl`
- Bench venv: `tony-omen:/tmp/vb` (torch-cpu, gliclass, fastapi)
- HF model cached: `heman10x/rlcd-modernbert-151m` (~600 MB) in omen `~/.cache/huggingface`

## Next actions suggested

1. Let the corpus grow (~200+ rows or a few weeks), meanwhile cap 4b CPU so it stops hurting Devin.
2. Fine-tune GLiClass on corpus + 4b-labeled augmentation → re-run this replay as the acceptance test (target: match 4b's 31/31 separation, pos ≥0.9 / neg ≤0.2).
3. Only then swap `ADA_JEV_URL` — keeping the same wire API means idc01 needs no code change.

# Orchestration conflict management — proposal

Date: 2026-09-27 · scope: Devin dispatches, Ada tool calls, job-run tasks
acting on shared resources (repos, dashboards, CMS pages, devices, hosts).

## Where conflicts bite today

| Conflict | Real example we hit |
|---|---|
| Same repo, two sessions | `pfg2-card.ts` duplicated render crash, version races → worktree-per-session rule |
| Same dashboard view | nobito + admin edits over websocket — last writer wins silently |
| Same device/entity | Ada voice toggles a plug while a job tests it |
| Same CMS slug | Ada republishes a page a dispatch session is regenerating |
| Same host lane | 3 sessions running heavy work on one host |
| Same deploy | concurrent `deploy-card.sh` — mitigated by `flock` today |

## Design: claim → check → act → release

### 1. Job claims (declared, durable)

Every dispatched/job-run task declares its **resource claims** in
`meta.json` + the job doc: `claims: [{repo: chaba, path: docs/kb/**},
{ha_view: chaba-home/nobito}, {host: tony-omen}, {device: switch.plug_tv}]`.

Dispatch wrapper derives defaults — `--repo chaba` implies
`{repo:chaba}`; `--host omen` implies `{host:omen}`.

### 2. Gate at dispatch time (not runtime)

`devin_dispatch` and `job-run start` check the job ledger first:

- **Conflict** (another `running`/`awaiting-user` job claims the same
  resource) → refuse with `conflict: job X holds repo:chaba` and let the
  caller decide: `queue` it (status `queued`, auto-starts when X closes),
  `proceed_anyway` (needs explicit confirmed), or cancel.
- Ada voice path: devin_dispatch already gates on confirmed — extend the
  deny message to name the conflicting job so Ada can tell Tony
  "job X owns chaba right now — queue it?"

### 3. Locks for hot single-writer resources

- `deploy-card.sh` already has `flock /tmp/pfg-deploy.lock` — keep.
- Dashboard mutations: `push-dashboard.py` gets a `--claim <view>` flag —
  the job doc records the view; a second mutation of the same view while
  a job holds it queues or fails loud.
- CMS slugs: `cms_publish_page` rejects if the slug is claimed by a
  running job (per-content-hash pending already exists — add claim check).

### 4. Ada voice commands vs running jobs

Voice is single-utterance — she shouldn't block. Rule:

- Voice command on a resource claimed by a running job → Ada answers
  "that's currently being changed by job X, want me to override?" —
  overrides go through the confirmed path and mark the job's doc
  `overridden_by: voice`.

### 5. Arbiter = this control desk

The foreground session is the arbiter: before dispatching N tasks, check
the ledger for overlapping claims and serialize them. The ledger query
(`devin_jobs`) already exists — extend it to return `claims` so a session
can plan a non-conflicting wave.

### 6. Resolution rules (documented precedence)

1. Explicit user instruction > everything
2. `awaiting-user` job + user answers → that job proceeds
3. Same-resource conflicts: first-claimed wins; second queues
4. Stale claims (`running` > 6h, no heartbeat) → auto-deny new writes,
   flag for review in the report feed

## What to build

| # | Piece | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `claims` on job docs + dispatch wrapper derives them | small |
| 2 | `devin_jobs` returns claims; Ada prompt: "check conflicts before dispatch" | small |
| 3 | Conflict gate in `devin_dispatch`/`job-run` (refuse/queue/proceed) | medium |
| 4 | `push-dashboard.py --claim` + view-level lock | small |
| 5 | stale-claim sweeper in dispatch-watch (heartbeat check) | small |

## Why this shape

Fits what exists: job docs are already the durable ledger, `flock` proves
the lock pattern, `devin_pending`/`devin_jobs` gives Ada visibility. No
new infra — claims ride on MDDB job docs, no central broker needed.

# รายงานสไตล์การสื่อสารฉบับปรับปรุง

**สถานะ:** บันทึกในโปรไฟล์ | **ภาษา:** ไทย/อังกฤษ (ตามบริบท)

## สรุปการเปลี่ยนแปลง
ผู้ใช้ต้องการให้ดิฉันใช้คำที่บอกช่วงเวลาแบบสัมพัทธ์ (Relative Time) แทนการระบุวันเวลาที่แน่นอน เพื่อให้อ่านง่ายและเข้าใจได้ทันทีในการโต้ตอบ โดยเฉพาะในภาษาไทย (และภาษาอังกฤษเมื่อเหมาะสม)

**ตัวอย่าง:**
- "1 ชั่วโมงที่แล้ว" (1 hour ago)
- "เมื่อเช้านี้" (This morning)
- "เมื่อวาน" (Yesterday)

**การดำเนินการ:**
ดิฉันได้บันทึกความชอบนี้ไว้ในโปรไฟล์ส่วนตัว และจะนำไปใช้ในการสื่อสารกับผู้ใช้ (User) ทุกครั้งที่มีการอ้างอิงถึงช่วงเวลาในอดีตเพื่อให้ง่ายต่อความเข้าใจ.

**สถานะปัจจุบัน:** กำลังตรวจสอบและแก้ไข

## ปัญหาที่พบ

- **การค้นหาประวัติการสนทนาขัดข้อง:** ระบบไม่สามารถค้นหาข้อมูลจากประวัติการสนทนาย้อนหลังตามคำขอของผู้ใช้ได้ โดยมีการแจ้งเตือนว่าข้อมูลในหน่วยความจำหลักเพียงพอแล้ว ทำให้ข้ามขั้นตอนการค้นหาเชิงลึก
- **เครื่องมือ Session Recall ทำงานไม่สำเร็จ:** เครื่องมือ `ada_session_recall` ไม่สามารถดึงข้อมูลที่ต้องการออกมาได้ หรือถูกบล็อกโดยกระบวนการตรวจสอบข้อมูลซ้อนซ้อน (Redundant Data Check)

## การดำเนินการ

- แจ้งให้ Devin ทราบเพื่อดำเนินการตรวจสอบเชิงลึกเกี่ยวกับสาเหตุที่เครื่องมือค้นหาหน่วยความจำทำงานไม่น่าเชื่อถือ
